newsitem.title: UK: EU monitoring BSkyB'S English soccer deal.
newsitem.headline: EU monitoring BSkyB'S English soccer deal.

text.p: The European Union's competition commissioner said on Thursday he was monitoring a television rights deal between BSkyB and English soccer's Premier League but had not called for a formal investigation into it.

A statement clarified commissioner Karel van Miert's position after the British Broadcasting Corporation put out a press release saying that Van Miert had called in an interview with BBC radio for a probe into the deal.
"He (Van Miert) wants to point out that a distinction has to be made between the need to closely watch all such deals and formal investigations," said the statement, issued through BSkyB.

"Such a formal investigation is presently underway as to the Dutch sports channel, especially as regards the seven-year duration of the contract and not as far as the BSkyB-Premier League (contract) is concerned," it added.

The European Commission launched a probe in August into a plan by the Dutch soccer association KNVB to give exclusive seven-year rights to British premier and first division matches to a new TV channel called Sport 7, which it partly owns.
BSkyB sealed a 670 million pound ($1.07 billion) contract in June this year to buy the rights to transmit Premier League soccer matches live until 2001.

"As to the BSkyB-Premiership contract, Van Miert said that this is part of a more general monitoring exercise related to the overall phenomnenon of exclusive TV rights on sports events," the statement added.
In the interview broadcast on BBC radio on Thursday night, Van Miert said: "We have to look into the (BSkyB-Premiership) deal and also the duration of the contract."

Asked if he would intervene in the deal, he replied, "We certainly will. We certainly will. And what should not happen is that those acquiring the rights will be in such a dominant position that they are going to impose the rules."
In a submission to the European Parliament last month, Van Miert signalled his concern over long-term sports deals involving ever-larger sums of money.
"There is this trend which seriously worries us that increasingly a few large groups can buy such (sports broadcasting) rights," he said.
BSkyB issued a statement criticising the BBC press release based on the interview, calling it a "blatant distortion of the facts".
